# NarrativeTrace .NET

Working with an AI agent? Paste this:

```text
Set up NarrativeTrace in this project and show me its first trace.
1. Read https://narrativetrace.ai/dotnet/llms.txt first. It carries the install block and the
known traps. Do not guess versions or artifact names.
2. If this directory has no project yet, create the smallest console app that
llms.txt's "Install and first trace" block describes. Otherwise work inside the existing
project and trace one real service boundary.
3. Install the CLI the way llms.txt shows, then run `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace
init --dry-run` and show me the diff. It installs the NarrativeTrace agent skills into this
project and adds a marked section to AGENTS.md. Run it for real only after I have seen the
diff.
4. If the `add-narrative-tracing` skill is now available, follow it. Otherwise follow the
"Install and first trace (copy this)" block in llms.txt.
5. Add one test that traces a call with a deny-listed parameter and asserts the trace shows
`[REDACTED]` for it.
6. Run the program, then run the doctor (`dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace doctor`).
Paste the trace and the doctor report, explain the trace in two sentences, and list exactly
what changed in the project.
Rules: never disable redaction; do not commit `.received.nt` files; run
everything in the foreground and read the output before you report; if you cannot fetch URLs,
say so and I will paste llms.txt.
```

> Code is the log. Auto-generate human-readable execution narratives from method names, parameter names, and return values — no manual logging.

## Install and first trace (copy this)

```bash
dotnet new console -n Hello && cd Hello
dotnet add package NarrativeTrace.Proxy
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install NarrativeTrace.Cli
```
<!-- snippet: examples/NarrativeTrace.Examples.SixtySeconds/Program.cs -->
```csharp
using NarrativeTrace.Core;
using NarrativeTrace.Proxy;
using NarrativeTrace.Runtime;

// snippet:begin fixedTraceparent
// A fixed W3C traceparent, seeded through NarrativeTraceConfig so this page's embedded output
// always names the same trace. A real run adopts nothing here (or a real inbound request header,
// via NarrativeTraceMiddleware) and gets a fresh, randomly generated trace id every time.
const string DemoTraceparent = "00-a1b2c3d4a1b2c3d4a1b2c3d4a1b2c3d4-a1b2c3d4a1b2c3d4-01";
// snippet:end fixedTraceparent

var context = new SyncNarrativeContext(
    new NarrativeTraceConfig(
        serviceIdentity: new ServiceIdentity("hello-service"), // names the service; unset, spans read unknown_service:dotnet
        initialTraceparent: Traceparent.Parse(DemoTraceparent)));
var orders = NarrativeTraceProxy.Create<IOrderService>(new OrderService(), context);

orders.PlaceOrder("cust-1", "book-123", 2);

Console.WriteLine(IndentedTextRenderer.Render(context.CaptureTrace()));

public interface IOrderService
{
    string PlaceOrder(string customerId, string productId, int quantity);
}

public sealed class OrderService : IOrderService
{
    public string PlaceOrder(string customerId, string productId, int quantity)
        => $"confirmed:{customerId}:{productId}:{quantity}";
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->
```bash
dotnet run
```
<!-- snippet: artifacts/sixty-seconds/see-a-trace.txt mask=duration -->
```text
trace: loose hook parks (a1b2c3d)

└── IOrderService.PlaceOrder(customerId: "cust-1", productId: "book-123", quantity: 2) → "confirmed:cust-1:book-123:2" — 6ms #1
```
<!-- /snippet -->
Then to your logger, same tree, two lines:
```csharp
using var loggerFactory = LoggerFactory.Create(b => b.AddConsole());
TraceLogExporter.ExportToLogger(context.CaptureTrace(), loggerFactory.CreateLogger("NarrativeTrace"));
```

Then prove the deny-list works. Same project, not a separate test project — the doctor below
only scans the directory it runs in, so a sibling test project would go unseen:
```bash
dotnet add package Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk
dotnet add package xunit
dotnet add package xunit.runner.visualstudio
dotnet add package NarrativeTrace.Testing.Xunit
```
<!-- snippet: tests/NarrativeTrace.Examples.SixtySeconds.Tests/RedactionQuickstartTests.cs -->
```csharp
using NarrativeTrace.Core;
using NarrativeTrace.Proxy;
using NarrativeTrace.TestingXunit;
using Xunit;

namespace NarrativeTrace.Examples.SixtySeconds.Tests;

public sealed class RedactionQuickstartTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void Redacts_a_deny_listed_parameter()
    {
        using var narrative = new NarrativeFixture();

        narrative.Run("pay with a deny-listed parameter", context =>
        {
            var account = NarrativeTraceProxy.Create<IAccountService>(new AccountService(), context);
            account.Pay("POL-123", "tok-super-secret-xyz");
        });

        var rendered = IndentedTextRenderer.Render(narrative.CaptureTrace());
        Assert.Contains("paymentToken: [REDACTED]", rendered);
        Assert.DoesNotContain("tok-super-secret-xyz", rendered);
    }
}

public interface IAccountService
{
    string Pay(string policyId, string paymentToken);
}

public sealed class AccountService : IAccountService
{
    public string Pay(string policyId, string paymentToken) => $"paid:{policyId}";
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->
```bash
dotnet test
```

## Runtime support

What the manifests declare, and what CI actually runs:

- **Tested:** the .NET 10 SDK on Linux. Every test project targets `net10.0`, and the gate runs on `ubuntu-latest` with SDK `10.0.301` (the version `global.json` pins). Windows and macOS are expected to work but have no CI job.
- **Declared, built, not run:** the libraries (`Core`, `Runtime`, `Proxy`, `DependencyInjection`, `Logging`, `Observability`, `Diagrams`, `Clarity`, `Glossary`) also compile for `netstandard2.0`, so they restore on .NET Framework and older .NET. No test executes that build, so treat it as expected to work, not tested.
- **`NarrativeTrace.AspNetCore` is `net10.0` only** and carries a framework reference to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App`: use it only in a project that runs on the ASP.NET Core shared framework. A console app or a worker without ASP.NET Core takes `Proxy` (or `DependencyInjection`) plus `Logging` or `Observability` instead.
- **`NarrativeTrace.Cli` is a `net10.0` .NET tool and `NarrativeTrace.MSBuild` a build-only shim.** Neither belongs in an application's runtime dependencies.
- **`NarrativeTrace.Legacy` is a deliberately empty reservation** of the `net48` slot. It has no API; do not reference it to get tracing on .NET Framework.
- **Not declared or tested:** trimming and Native AOT. Capture is built on `System.Reflection.DispatchProxy`, so do not assume either works.

## Before you start
- `NarrativeTrace.Proxy` pulls in `.Runtime`+`.Core`.
- `NARRATIVETRACE_OUTPUT` defaults **on**.
- `new ProxyOptions(Redaction: ...)` reaches the proxy, and `NarrativeTracingDiOptions.Redaction`/`NarrativeTraceOptions.Redaction` reach DI auto-wrap and ASP.NET Core auto-wrapped proxies too.
- **Name the service.** Spans carry the service name you give them; unset, every span is attributed to `unknown_service:dotnet` on the platform and in OpenTelemetry, and NarrativeTrace never guesses one from the assembly. Set `NARRATIVETRACE_SERVICE_NAME` (with `NARRATIVETRACE_SERVICE_VERSION` and `NARRATIVETRACE_ENVIRONMENT`), or build the identity in code as the first trace above does (`new ServiceIdentity("hello-service")`). The xUnit fixture, the NUnit base and `AddNarrativeTracing` read the variables; `NarrativeTracingDiOptions.ServiceIdentity`, `NarrativeTraceOptions.ServiceIdentity` or `NarrativeTrace:ServiceName` in `appsettings.json` set it in code (the ASP.NET Core registration never reads the variables), and code beats the environment. The doctor's `config.service-identity` fails when non-test code wires tracing and names no service. See [Configuration Guide, Service identity](configuration.md#service-identity).
- **Span names.** A proxy is built on an interface, and its spans are named after the interface (`IOrderService.PlaceOrder`); `NarrativeTraceProxy.Create<T>` rejects a class, so no traced target is ever without a type name. To name a span differently pass `new ProxyOptions(ClassName: "OrderService")`; calling `EnterMethod(className, ...)` by hand uses the name you pass.
- **Parameter names.** NarrativeTrace reads parameter names by reflection from the interface method: no compiler flag, nothing to pass. The one case it cannot: a method whose metadata carries no names (an interface emitted at run time), which renders as `arg0`, `arg1` — put `[Traced("customerId", "productId")]` on that method.
- The `.nt` structural artifact is a last-green baseline with per-invocation identity, `manifest.json` and approval mode: `NARRATIVETRACE_APPROVAL=true` fails a passing test whose structure differs from its committed `*.approved.nt`, and `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace approve` promotes a reviewed `*.received.nt`. See [Structural Trace Format](../structural-trace-format.md).
- A trace has a name (`trace: bold elk soars (a1b2c3d)`, above), and a test-suite run has one too — the console footer, `manifest.json`'s `run` object, the Markdown frontmatter's `run:` field, and `nt.runName` in the logging bridge's scope. Neither ever reaches the `.nt` text. See [Configuration Guide §7](configuration.md#7-logging-bridge-microsoftextensionslogging).
- Every `NARRATIVETRACE_*` variable — what it sets, its default, and a runnable example of the effect — is tabulated in [Configuration Guide §10](configuration.md#10-environment-variable-worked-examples).

## Tracing a request in production

The test path above stays; this is the one for a running ASP.NET Core service.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNarrativeTrace(builder.Configuration);
builder.Services.AddNarrativeTracing(o => o.Namespaces("MyApp.Services"));
// ...
app.UseMiddleware<NarrativeTraceMiddleware>();
```

- **Exclusions:** `AddNarrativeTracing` never traces generated code (compiler-generated, dynamic-assembly and `DispatchProxy` types), and leaves a shipped default list of framework, mocking and test-runner namespaces alone even when included; `ExcludeNamespaces(...)` or `NARRATIVETRACE_EXCLUDE` (`;`-separated) replaces that list as a whole and always wins over `Namespaces(...)`. See [Dependency Injection guide](dependency-injection.md#instrumentation-exclusions).
- **Per-request context:** `AddNarrativeTrace` registers a *scoped* `INarrativeContext` (a `SyncNarrativeContext`), so each request gets its own and concurrent requests do not mix. The middleware stores it in `HttpContext.Items`; read it with `HttpContext.GetNarrativeContext()`. Services wrapped by `AddNarrativeTracing` resolve the same scoped context, so their calls nest into the request's trace.
- **Where the trace is captured:** inside the middleware, in a `finally` after the rest of the pipeline returns, with the response status and elapsed milliseconds. A request that throws still produces a trace (status 500 unless an error status was already set). Work started with a `Task` during the request lands in that same trace. Put the middleware where you want the clock to start: it traces what runs after it.
- **Cleanup:** the middleware never calls `Reset()`; the context is discarded with the request's DI scope. You do not reset a request's context yourself. Excluded paths (`options.ExcludedPaths.Add("/health")`) create no context and no trace.
- **Failure isolation:** a fault while stamping the request or inside the exporter is swallowed; it never fails the request.
- **Level:** defaults to `Detail`. Set `NarrativeTrace:Level` in configuration or `options.Level` to lower it in production.
- **Exporter, built in:** `LoggerTraceExporter` (package `NarrativeTrace.AspNetCore`, the default) writes one `Information` entry per request — `GET /api/orders [200] 42ms — {json}` — to the logger category `NarrativeTrace.Export`. Values in it are already redacted.
- **Exporter, logger tree:** `TraceLogExporter.ExportToLogger(tree, logger)` (package `NarrativeTrace.Logging`, namespace `NarrativeTrace.Logging`) writes the indented call tree, one record per node, from a trace you captured yourself.
- **Exporter, OpenTelemetry:** `TraceActivityExporter.Export(tree)` (package `NarrativeTrace.Observability`, namespace `NarrativeTrace.Observability`) replays a finished trace as `Activity` spans under the source `"NarrativeTrace"`; register it with `.AddSource("NarrativeTrace")`. The middleware has no built-in OpenTelemetry exporter: register your own `ITraceExporter` that calls it. Register it before `AddNarrativeTrace`, which only adds its default when none is present:

```csharp
public sealed class OtelTraceExporter : ITraceExporter
{
    public void Export(TraceTree tree, RequestContext request) => TraceActivityExporter.Export(tree);
}

builder.Services.AddSingleton<ITraceExporter, OtelTraceExporter>();
builder.Services.AddNarrativeTrace(builder.Configuration);
```

The exported spans carry the same (redacted) values as the trace, so mind where the OpenTelemetry pipeline ships them. See the [ASP.NET Core Guide](aspnetcore.md#3-export).

## Privacy and redaction

See [Privacy and Redaction](../privacy-and-redaction.md) for what is redacted on every surface and what outranks it. In short:

- **Names:** a deny-list of case-insensitive name patterns in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Chinese and German (for example `password`, `token`, `contrasena`, `senha`, `rut`, `dni`, `cpf`); a matching parameter, property or field is replaced by `[REDACTED]` before its value is read.
- **Value shapes:** whatever the field is called, a JWT, a Luhn-valid payment card number, a `Set-Cookie` string, and a national identity number that passes its own check digits (RUT, CPF, CNPJ, Spanish DNI/NIE, French NIR, Chinese resident ID, dashed US SSN) are redacted. `[NotTraced]` always wins and renders the same `[REDACTED]` marker; the structural `.nt` artifact holds no values at all.
- **No off switch you can reach by accident:** no environment variable, flag or MSBuild property turns redaction off. The integrations take a `RedactionPolicy` (`ProxyOptions`, `NarrativeTracingDiOptions`, `NarrativeTraceOptions`), and only passing `RedactionPolicy.Disabled` there disables the name and value-shape rules, in your own source. `NARRATIVETRACE_REDACTION_ADDITIONALPATTERNS` can only add patterns. The xUnit and NUnit helpers accept no policy.

## Agent skills
- `narrativetrace-doctor` — Diagnoses a NarrativeTrace .NET install without changing anything: runs the doctor CLI and explains every failing check and its fix — including whether the NarrativeTrace agent skills are installed and current — proves redaction with a real test, opens the newest rendered trace before trusting any assertion against it, and — flagged unstudied — walks an approval-trace diff.
- `add-narrative-tracing` — Adds NarrativeTrace to a .NET project end to end: installs the real toolchain with a frozen restore, wraps a service and renders its first trace, sends the trace to a logger with one call, finishes by running the doctor CLI to confirm the install, and ends by previewing the agent skills install so the next session finds them.
- `narrativetrace-feedback` — Reports a defect in NarrativeTrace itself — the library, the doctor, an agent skill, or the published install prompt. Drafts the report from this project (the install coordinates, the doctor's own JSON report, and at most one structural trace), refuses to write one that carries a value from your traces and names the rule that refused it, shows you the whole draft, and then asks once whether to file it publicly. Files nothing without your answer and sends nothing anywhere.
- `add-narrativetrace-clarity` — Adds or verifies NarrativeTrace Clarity in a .NET project. Use when you want a first static naming report, per-element explanations, or an explicit clarity quality gate. Runs the real `clarity-scan` and `clarity-check` verbs, checks fresh nonempty JSON and Markdown, applies the report's renames and re-runs until the gate is clean, and preserves existing thresholds.
- `narrativetrace-verify` — Verifies a change in a .NET project by reading what the code actually did before saying it is done. Writes the intent down first, runs the smallest real path, reads the value-free structural trace against the intent and opens values only on the span that looks wrong, then pins the flow as an approval baseline behind your yes and reports what the trace showed, citing span ids. Skips itself, saying why, for a pure function or a one-class edit.
- `narrativetrace-debug` — Finds the cause of a wrong result in a .NET project by reading what the code did with the values, not by stepping through it. Reproduces the symptom with NarrativeTrace on, names the first span where a value diverges by its span id, fixes it there and checks the structural trace shows nothing else moved, then pins the reproduction as a regression test and an approval baseline behind your yes. Hands a defect in NarrativeTrace itself to `narrativetrace-feedback`.
- `narrativetrace-explain` — Explains what an application or a flow actually does, with nothing broken and no change needing verification. Decides first whether a trace is worth it: a question ten lines of source answer is answered from the source, with no install and no run. Otherwise it runs one existing test or entry point for the flow, reads the value-free structural trace, and explains the run by span id, marking what it inferred and naming the code no span covered. Hands a defect to `narrativetrace-debug`, a change to `narrativetrace-verify`.

Install them into this project: `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace init --dry-run`, read the diff, then run it again without `--dry-run`; it writes `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` (the directory Claude Code loads; `--vendor none` leaves it out). See [Agent Skills](../agent-skills.md) for the full walkthrough and `uninstall`. Each platform's install path (Cursor, Replit, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code), what its agent finds, and the small pointer file `init` writes for it are in [Use NarrativeTrace with your agent](../use-with-your-agent.md).

They are also reachable from two registries, each landing the same pages `init` then adopts. The Claude Code plugin marketplace carries them too: `/plugin marketplace add narrativetrace/narrativetrace-dotnet`, then `/plugin install narrativetrace-dotnet@narrativetrace-dotnet` — then run `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace init --dry-run`, read the diff, and run it without the flag so `AGENTS.md` points at them. `npx skills add narrativetrace/narrativetrace-dotnet` installs the open-standard pages directly into the project — then run `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace init --dry-run`, read the diff, and run it without the flag so `AGENTS.md` points at them.

## Doctor
Confirm the install and surface misconfigurations — among its nineteen checks, one per framework this project uses (the doctor detects which, and each failing fix prints the compiled wiring lines) and whether the agent skills above are installed and current (`config.skills-installed`):
```bash
dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace doctor
```
<!-- covered-frameworks:begin -->
Covered frameworks (each row of the doctor's framework table): ASP.NET Core (`config.registration-pair`); Dependency injection (`config.di-namespaces`); xUnit (`config.xunit-fixture`); NUnit (`config.nunit-base`); OpenTelemetry (`config.otel-source`); Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (`trap.silent-sink`); MSBuild clarity targets (owned by the add-narrativetrace-clarity skill).
<!-- covered-frameworks:end -->

If the install block above didn't make the tool available, add it first: `dotnet tool install --global NarrativeTrace.Cli` (then invoke it as `dotnet-narrativetrace doctor`).

## Report a problem

If NarrativeTrace, this file, a skill or the doctor is wrong, ask your agent to use the `narrativetrace-feedback` skill: it drafts the report from your project, refuses to write one that carries a value from your traces, shows you the whole thing, and files nothing until you say so. Nothing is sent anywhere — the draft is yours until you submit it yourself.

```bash
dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace doctor --report
dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace feedback draft --category doctor --step <check id> --did "..." --happened "..." --expected "..."
```

That writes the draft and its body under `TestResults/narrativetrace/feedback/`, and exits 2 naming a `vf.*` rule if a field carries a value instead of a description. `feedback url` then prints the pre-filled issue form for `github.com/narrativetrace/narrativetrace-dotnet`, which you open and submit under your own account; `feedback gh` prints the `gh issue create` line when `gh` is signed in. Filing is public: it shows that your project uses NarrativeTrace.

## Recipes

One page per problem, in the words a user would type. Each page carries its scenario's code and the real output of a run this build performs — nothing on a recipe page is typed by hand.

- [Add logging to this service](../recipes/add-logging-to-this-service.md) — a checkout with no log statement: wrap its collaborators once and every call, with its parameter names and its result, appears in the project's own `ILogger`.
- [Help me debug and fix this bug](../recipes/help-me-debug-and-fix-this-bug.md) — a declined card leaves the stock reserved: the failing run's narrative shows `Reserve`, then `Charge` throwing, then nothing, and the fix and the approved baseline that pins it.
- [Why did this test fail](../recipes/why-did-this-test-fail.md) — a red checkout test read span by span against the assertion, where every span agrees with every other and the expectation is what is stale.
- [Review a complex flow before changing it](../recipes/review-a-complex-flow-before-changing-it.md) — one run at `Detail` and at `Summary`, with the log line that carries values beside the value-free `.nt` an agent reads.
- [Review a refactoring: did behaviour change](../recipes/review-a-refactoring-did-behaviour-change.md) — the tests stay green, the approval diff names the dropped call, and `dotnet tool run dotnet-narrativetrace approve` is how you say yes.
- [Follow one request across services (distributed tracing)](../recipes/follow-one-request-across-services.md) — the checkout charges through a second traced service over a real socket: the W3C `traceparent` rides with the request, so one trace id is in both services' lines and the callee's root names the caller's span as its parent.
- [Keep secrets out of the logs](../recipes/keep-secrets-out-of-the-logs.md) — a password caught by its parameter name and a card number caught by its value, in the log and in the trace, with the test that reads the log back as the proof.
- [Follow a flow across threads](../recipes/follow-a-flow-across-threads.md) — two branches of a `ForkJoinGroup` keep the customer's trace id and come home under the span that launched them; the same work handed to a worker without the group is a detached second root.
- [Send traces to the observability stack you already run](../recipes/send-traces-to-the-observability-stack-you-already-run.md) — one run, two consumers: the narrative lines your logger already writes beside the OpenTelemetry spans the same events became, attribute by attribute, redactions included.
- [Trace in production without the cost](../recipes/trace-in-production-without-the-cost.md) — one declined checkout rendered at `Detail` and at `Errors`, where a run that succeeded writes no artifact at all, and only `Off` skips interception.

## Target frameworks

Libraries multi-target `net10.0` and `netstandard2.0` (the `Legacy`
package adds `net48`). No compiler flag is needed — .NET retains parameter
names in metadata by default.

## Packages (NuGet id = project name)

- `NarrativeTrace.Core` — trace model, `INarrativeContext`, config, redaction, text/Markdown/prose renderers; namespace `NarrativeTrace.Core.Annotation` holds `[Narrated]`/`[OnError]`/`[NotTraced]`/`[NarrativeSummary]`
- `NarrativeTrace.Runtime` — capture engine (`SyncNarrativeContext`, `AsyncNarrativeContext`), JSON/chapter exporters
- `NarrativeTrace.Proxy` — `NarrativeTraceProxy.Create`, `[Traced]`
- `NarrativeTrace.DependencyInjection` — `AddNarrativeTracing` namespace auto-wrap
- `NarrativeTrace.AspNetCore` — per-request middleware, `ITraceExporter`
- `NarrativeTrace.Logging` — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` bridge
- `NarrativeTrace.Observability` — OpenTelemetry (`ActivitySource` "NarrativeTrace", batch + live)
- `NarrativeTrace.Diagrams` — Mermaid / PlantUML sequence renderers
- `NarrativeTrace.Clarity` — naming-clarity analysis and reporting
- `NarrativeTrace.Cli` — `dotnet-narrativetrace` global tool (`doctor`, `init`, `uninstall`, `clarity-scan`, `clarity-aggregate`, `clarity-check`, `glossary`)
- `NarrativeTrace.MSBuild` — build-only shim wiring the CLI into `dotnet build`/`test`
- `NarrativeTrace.Testing.Xunit` / `.NUnit` — per-test context + failure-narrative printing

**Install every `NarrativeTrace.*` package at one version.** Each package declares its NarrativeTrace dependencies as a minimum version equal to the version it was built at (NuGet's `>=`), not an exact pin and not a wide range, so NuGet will accept a mix of an older and a newer package. Mixed versions are not tested together; install them together at the same version.

## Core API

- `new SyncNarrativeContext(new NarrativeTraceConfig(TracingLevel.Detail))`
- `NarrativeTraceProxy.Create<T>(target, context)` → traced proxy
- `context.CaptureTrace()` → `TraceTree`; `context.Reset()`
- `IndentedTextRenderer.Render(tree)` / `MarkdownRenderer.Render(tree)` / `ProseRenderer.Render(tree)`
- `MarkdownRenderer.RenderDocument(tree, metadata)` — frontmatter + `## Trace:` header + call flow (what per-test `.md` artifacts contain)
- `TracingLevel`: `Off`, `Errors`, `Summary`, `Narrative`, `Detail`

## Configuration

- Env: `NARRATIVETRACE_LEVEL`, `NARRATIVETRACE_OUTPUT`, `NARRATIVETRACE_OUTPUT_DIR`, `NARRATIVETRACE_FORMAT`, `NARRATIVETRACE_APPROVAL`, `NARRATIVETRACE_APPROVED_DIR` (`ConfigResolver`, invalid values degrade to defaults)
- DI: `services.AddNarrativeTracing(o => o.Namespaces("MyApp.Services"))`
- ASP.NET Core: `services.AddNarrativeTrace(configuration)` + `app.UseMiddleware<NarrativeTraceMiddleware>()`; trace services via `HttpContext.GetNarrativeContext()`; send the trace on outbound HTTP calls with `services.AddHttpClient(name).AddNarrativeTraceTraceparentPropagation()` (or `TraceparentHeaders.Current(context)` without a factory)
- MSBuild: `NarrativeTrace.MSBuild` package → `ClarityScan`/`ClarityCheck` targets

## Clarity

- `ClarityScanner.Scan([typeof(T)])` (reflection-only) or `ClarityAnalyzer.Analyze(tree)`
- Five weighted components: Method 30%, Parameter 25%, Class 20%, Structural 15%, Cohesion 10%
- CI gate: `dotnet-narrativetrace clarity-scan --assembly X.dll --output-dir narrativetrace` then `clarity-check --results narrativetrace/clarity-scan-results.json --min-score 0.8 --max-high-issues 0`

## Examples

- `examples/NarrativeTrace.Examples.ECommerce` — nested order-flow narrative (success, declined payment, out of stock) + clear-vs-cryptic naming comparison

## Field notes from AI agents (self-reported, not a benchmark)
We asked AI agents to build a claims service with NarrativeTrace and write up the experience for another engineer, naming what was awkward. Prompted, one run each, unedited, model named; we wrote the library. The reports so far are from elsewhere in the NarrativeTrace family; the same exercise runs for .NET next, and the principle they describe — the trace as evidence, redaction by parameter name, output on by default — is the same here.
